root_idea.summary: The root centers on one thing standing apart from, recoiling from, or failing to adhere to another.
root_idea.development: The basic notion of non-adherence develops into physical withdrawal and separation, avoidance or rejection, social coarseness, driving away or casting off, and the image of refuse discharged by flowing water.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic imperfect is normalized to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form تَجَافَى.

senses.definition: To draw away, rise apart, or withdraw from something.
senses.usage_conditions: In the supplied Quran occurrence, the construction تَجَافَى عَنْ describes the sides or bodies of people withdrawing from their beds; the preposition عَنْ marks the place or thing from which one withdraws.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fail to rest upon or adhere to its place; to heave, rise, or stand apart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a side upon a bed, a saddle upon an animal, and similar things that do not remain settled in their proper position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recoil, shrink, or be averse from something, and consequently avoid or neglect it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This usage includes recoiling from matters of knowledge or science.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be thick, coarse, rough, or harsh in texture or make.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a garment or piece of cloth and to the nib of a reed pen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become coarse, rough, or rude in disposition, or to treat others coarsely and unkindly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage covers rudeness or hardness of character and rough, churlish, uncivil, or surly dealings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become heavy, burdensome, oppressive, or onerous to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Constructed with the burden or matter that weighs upon the person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cast forth or drive away, as froth from a cooking-pot or things carried by a torrent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a discharge or expulsion usage, distinct from merely withdrawing from a place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn away from, avoid, shun, or drive away a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage may convey hatred or aversion when directed toward a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fail to keep, hold fast, or attend to something; to neglect it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is used both of failing to hold fast to property and of neglecting to care for or attend to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To do what displeases, grieves, or vexes someone; to do him harm or evil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This describes conduct judged injurious or hateful to the person affected.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The causing, ordering, or directing of coarse, rough, or rude treatment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun associated with making someone act or behave harshly toward another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause something to be apart from, raised from, or not resting upon another thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of raising a body part from a resting surface, setting the upper arms apart from the sides, or raising a saddle from an animal's back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or cause someone or something to become distant, remote, far off, or aloof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use of making an object or person distant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fatigue livestock by driving them vehemently without allowing them to feed adequately.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction refers to exhausting cattle through harsh driving and withholding or failing to provide feed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land, to become stripped of its good and reduced to the condition of refuse cast forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of land whose productive substance has departed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To relinquish or give another person his right or due.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended usage in which withdrawing from a claim signifies yielding it to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline, decline, or turn from side to side, including turning from right toward wrong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This describes repeated or directional deviation rather than simple physical removal from a resting place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove a person or thing from its place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive removal from the original position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To regard or judge a bed or similar object to be thick, coarse, or rough.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object assessed as coarse is typically a bed or comparable furnishing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To demand or require of someone that he do what is displeasing, grievous, vexatious, or evil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative-demand construction centered on requiring objectionable conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become coarse, rough, rude, unkind, hard, churlish, uncivil, or surly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes the acquisition or manifestation of a harsh disposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single act or instance of coarse, rough, rude, unkind, or surly treatment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes an individual occurrence of harsh or discourteous behavior.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Coarseness, roughness, or rudeness, whether in make or in one's dealings with others; unkindness or hardness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is opposed to kindness or good treatment and can describe a prevailing quality in social intercourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The roughness or hardship inflicted by time or fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage in which adversity is portrayed as striking or afflicting a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The rubbish, froth, or scum cast forth by a valley torrent or by a cooking-pot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This noun denotes material discharged and left aside by flowing water or boiling contents.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first or foremost of a group of people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application likening the foremost people to what is driven forward by a torrent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thick, coarse, or rough.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a garment, bed, or similar object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person coarse or rough in constitution, disposition, or dealings; rude, unkind, hard, or surly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle can describe physical make as well as harsh conduct toward companions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Obdurate or unresponsive toward admonition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَنْ in the construction جَافٍ عَنِ الْمَوْعِظَةِ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Physical non-adherence or rising from a place.
Coarseness of cloth or a pen nib.
Casting forth froth or driving away by a torrent.
Turning away, shunning, or driving away a person.
Failure to hold fast to property.
Causing something to rise apart or be raised.
Fatiguing livestock by harsh driving and lack of feed.
Land becoming stripped of its good.
Physical withdrawal is Quran-attested; relinquishing a right is a distinct extended usage.
Turning or deviating from side to side or from right to wrong.
Judging a bed or similar object coarse.
A single act of rude treatment.
Rudeness or coarseness, including its figurative application to adversity.
Rudeness of a person and obduracy toward admonition.
